ai.description: Ristella rurkii is a small skink reaching 45 mm. It features a bronze-brown dorsum, a dark lateral stripe, and a distinctively pale, unspotted venter. It is identified by its reduced, four-fingered limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ristella rurkii* is best distinguished by its lack of a distinct light-colored dorsolateral stripe, which is consistently present in all other Indian *Ristella* species.
ai.habitat: Ristella rurkii inhabits the leaf litter of moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Ristella rurkii is a diurnal lizard that actively forages for small invertebrates among leaf litter, relying on its agility to escape potential threats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ristella rurkii* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ristella rurkii* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
